newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria parliament approves stop-gap budget bill.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria parliament approves stop-gap budget bill.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament approved on Friday a stop-gap budget bill to service large government debt payments and finance public spending until a viable 1997 budget is passed, officials said.

"The deficit assumed in the bill was limited to the amount of interest payments due on government debt," Kiril Zhelev, head of the parliament's budget committee said during Friday's parliament session. He declined to elaborate.
The bill was approved only by deputies from the ruling Socialist party. The opposition has boycotted parliament since January 10 to press its demand for early general elections.
The bill provided for a 100-percent increase in public employees' salaries, pensions and social benefits.
Under the bill, state debt would be refinanced through new government securities issues and a direct 20-year loan from the central bank. The amount of the credit was not specified.

"The bill provides a legal basis for the central bank to extend direct loans to the government. Without it, the bank could reject further refinancing to the goverment," a central bank board member, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

In December, the central bank extended a 15-year 115 billion lev ($63.9 million) loan to the government to bridge a budget gap in line with the second revision of the 1996 budget approved by parliament, saying the loan would boost inflation.
"We had expressed our position, and we would not be willing to make a new statement," the central bank board member said.

Servicing the huge state debt has become a major problem for the the government which spent some 162 billion levs out of a revenue of 175 billion levs this month on interest payments, trade minister Atanas Paparizov said on Thursday.
Domestic debt surged to 1,053 billion levs in December from 345 billion levs a year earlier.
A slump in the lev and soaring inflation since then have made unrealistic the assumptions made in the 1997 draft budget approved by the outgoing Socialist cabinet at the beginning of January.
The draft assumed a lev/dollar rate of 500, implementation of a fixed exchange rate system and a deficit of 6.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). GDP was estimated at 4.585 trillion levs.

The lev fell to 1,930-2,000 on Friday from around 600 at the beginning of the month. Inflation for the first half of January was 30.8 percent and was seen near 50 percent at the end of the month. -- Sofia Newsroom +359 2 981 8569 ($ = 1800 Bulgarian Levs)
